proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571 reaches 1 in fewer than 182 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 182.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, the stopping time of n is less than 182.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 34 modulo 17.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, n^2 equals (n^2) + [n = 3].
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, n^2 is at least n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571 for which n^2 > 1571.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1571, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
The steps above establish the statement up to 1571, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 1571.
